title: Ambient Prefetch Circuitry SDK - PRD Draft
summary: Proposal for an SDK-driven prefetched streaming model that surface ambient partial results, lightweight session snapshots, and a deterministic tool-call election mechanism to reduce tail latency and improve developer ergonomics for structured outputs.
background: We have many incremental streaming proposals in product but no single lightweight SDK pattern that blends client prefetch, server-side snapshotting, and deterministic tool selection. Teams building multi-tool orchestrations are seeing high tail latencies and inconsistent structured outputs across flaky networks. This draft experiments with an "ambient prefetch" concept: SDKs proactively request low-cost partial predictions and small state snapshots that can be rehydrated to resume higher-fidelity generations or tool calls with lower end-to-end latency.
goals: 1) Reduce 95th/99th percentile latency for tool-heavy streaming calls by 20–40% for mobile/edge clients. 2) Provide a small, ergonomic SDK surface that makes prefetch opt-in and safe. 3) Make structured output (JSON-like frames) more stable under partial/resume scenarios. 4) Ensure predictable billing semantics and clear telemetry to measure unit economics.
non_goals: 1) Replace full session persistence or offline-first SDKs. 2) Ship heavy client-side model execution. 3) Solve every edge-case of tool conflict resolution; aim for deterministic, auditable heuristics instead.
personas: Frontend engineer embedding Chat + tool calls into mobile app (needs low tail latency)
Platform engineer building a bounded-cost connector that uses Hosted API with dedicated capacity
SDK engineer who must maintain a tiny dependency and clear upgrade path
user_stories: As a mobile frontend engineer, I want the SDK to return an actionable partial summary quickly so the UI can show early results while the full tool call completes.
As a payments integrator, I want deterministic tool election so two retries don't trigger duplicate downstream actions.
As an SRE, I want telemetry that ties prefetch events to cost and latency so we can decide default settings for customers.
requirements: R1: SDK exposes a single opt-in prefetched() flag per session and per-route.
R2: Server supports lightweight snapshot tokens (opaque, short TTL) that capture prefix KV cache + model variant fingerprint.
R3: Streaming contract can emit 'ambient' frames that are low-fidelity but safe to render.
R4: Tool-call election algorithm is deterministic based on session token + call-hash and returns a conflict code if multiple competing toollets map to the same resource.
R5: Billing: ambient prefetch tokens cost at most 10% of equivalent full-call cost; clear meterings in response metadata.
R6: Observable events for prefetch start/finish/resume/errors with sampleable traces and token counts.
R7: SDK fallback: if snapshot resume fails, SDK must surface a graceful retry path that avoids double-calling tools.
R8: Structured output schema versioned; partial frames include schema-version + path hints to allow client incremental merging.
api_surface: New top-level SDK options: prefetched: boolean, snapshot_ttl_seconds: integer, ambient_frame_threshold_ms: integer. Response metadata fields: snapshot_token, ambient_frame: {type, confidence_est}, billing_hint. New server headers: X-Ambient-Variant, X-Prefetch-Charge.
streaming_contract:
- Stream frames are typed: control, ambient, progressive, final.
- Ambient frames are guaranteed to be prefix-only and must not contain irreversible side-effect directives.
- Progressive frames can escalate to final frames if resumed.
- Clients may request resume by passing snapshot_token in subsequent call.
- If server cannot produce ambient frames quickly, it should send a lightweight heartbeat control frame indicating estimated time-to-first-ambient.
- Frame delivery guarantees: ordered, idempotent replayable on resume using snapshot_token.
tool_calling_flow:
1) Initial call with prefetched=true -> server returns ambient frames and snapshot_token. 2) Client displays ambient result. 3) If client wants definitive tool action, it sends resume request with snapshot_token and tool-intent header. 4) Server runs deterministically selected tool based on election rules (call-hash + token). 5) Server returns tool call result as progressive/final frames; if election conflict, returns conflict control frame and suggested resolution.
Special rules: tool calls cannot be performed in ambient-only phase; only via resume to avoid accidental side effects. SDK helper will wrap resume+idempotency token creation for developer convenience.
structured_output_schema:
- Base is JSON-lines frames with 'frame_type' and 'schema_version' fields.
- Partial frames include 'path_hints' (array) and 'confidence_estimates' to allow client merging.
- Schema evolution: server includes 'deprecated_paths' list in metadata when rolling changes.
- Validation: SDK exposes a lightweight validator that can accept partial frames and merge them into an in-memory representation; mismatches produce 'soft-fail' diagnostics but not hard errors unless in strict mode.
sdk_ergonomics_guidelines:
- Keep API surface tiny: one new config object on client creation.
- Provide high-level helpers: prefetchableRoute(route, options), resumeSnapshot(token, toolIntent).
- Expose event hooks: onAmbient(frame), onProgress(frame), onResumeError(err).
- Defaults tuned for mobile: prefetched=false, ambient_frame_threshold_ms=120, snapshot_ttl_seconds=30.
- Bundle small polyfills for offline merge helpers; do not pull large deps.
- Document explicit developer patterns for safe tool invocation and idempotency.
telemetry_and_observability:
- Emit metrics: ambient_frames_per_route, snapshot_issues, resume_latency_p50/95/99, prefetch_cost_ratio.
- Tracing spans: prefetch:start, prefetch:end, snapshot:issue, resume:start, tool:election.
- Billing tagging on token usage so UI can show customers ambient vs final token consumption.
- Alerts: sudden increase in resume failures or elevated conflict rates for a route should trigger investigations.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (experiment): small beta with 3 customers and internal apps; collect telemetry and correctness logs.
Phase 1: expose SDK opt-in to all customers as 'experimental' flag; default off.
Phase 2: enable on selected low-variance routes for all customers with opt-out.
Phase 3: graduate to GA after 3 months of stable metrics and documented cost models.
Backout: if resume conflict rate > 0.5% or billing overrun exceeds forecast, feature toggled off at route level.
open_questions: Q1: How do we set a hard cost cap for ambient prefetches to prevent abuse?
Q2: What TTL is appropriate for snapshot_token in cross-region resume scenarios?
Q3: Should ambient frames be allowed to include high-confidence tool suggestions (non-executing) or are they strictly read-only?
Q4: How do we support customers who require cryptographic signing of snapshot tokens for private deployments?
Q5: Does the deterministic tool election need to be stable across model variant upgrades or scoped to snapshot fingerprints?
reviewer_notes: This is intentionally pragmatic: focus on developer ergonomics and measurable tail-latency wins. Keep prefetch conservative initially to limit billing ambiguity. Ask infra to validate that snapshot tokens do not increase DB pressure. Feedback wanted on default timeouts and API naming.
